summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining global local attention, transformer architectures, and decoder structures for audio-visual speech separation and sequence processing. Drawing on evidence of high parameter counts and computational costs in existing models, the approach integrates global-local attention blocks into each layer of a lightweight encoder-decoder separator. According to the DVF assessment, this combination receives a feasibility score of 2.0, a desirability score of 5.0, and a viability score of 4.0, with feasibility identified as the riskiest axis.

target_user.text: The target users are unverified based on the available bundle evidence.

jtbd.text: The job to be done is to perform audio-visual speech separation or related sequence processing tasks while reducing computational costs and parameter counts.

value_prop.text: This combination provides an efficient, lightweight encoder-decoder separator that incorporates global-local attention blocks in each layer to capture multi-scale dependencies with lower computational overhead.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption, driven by feasibility axis score 2.0, is that integrating global-local attention into every layer of a lightweight decoder architecture can be trained stably without exceeding target hardware latency or memory limits.

mvp.text: As a technical proof of concept from existing packages, the MVP will build a small-scale encoder-decoder script using open-source libraries to measure inference latency and parameter size against a baseline.
mvp.type: technical proof of concept from existing packages

success_metric.text: Success will be measured by achieving a proposed threshold: greater than 50 percent reduction in parameters and a proposed threshold: over 2x reduction in MACs compared to baseline architectures while maintaining separation quality.

kill_criteria.text: The approach is killed if the prototype exceeds a proposed threshold: 50 milliseconds of processing latency per frame or fails to demonstrate any MAC reduction.
